changes.historical_text: You can pay 500 Life Points to Special Summon this card when "Pyramid of Light" is on the field. This card cannot attack during the turn that it is Normal Summoned or Special Summoned. This card cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard. If this card destroys a Defense Position monster as a result of battle, inflict damage to your opponent's Life Points equal to half of the ATK of the destroyed monster.
changes.modern_text: You can pay 500 Life Points to Special Summon this card when "Pyramid of Light" is on the field. This card cannot attack during the turn that it is Normal Summoned or Special Summoned. This card cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard. If this card destroys a Defense Position monster as a result of battle, inflict damage to your opponent's Life Points equal to half of the ATK of the destroyed monster.
changes.summary: Era trigger timing encoded per card (upstream annotation: "Battle destroyed registers while the mo[n]ster is on field"): the goat script hangs the burn on EVENT_BATTLED with condition `other:IsBattleDestroyed() and other:IsPosition(POS_DEFENSE)`, so it registers off the damage-calculation event and never asks whether Andro Sphinx itself still relates to the battle; the modern script uses EVENT_BATTLE_DESTROYING and requires `c:IsRelateToBattle()` plus the victim's battle position. In play the era version still inflicts the half-base-ATK burn when Andro Sphinx leaves the field or is destroyed in the same battle, and it reads the destroyed monster's current position rather than its battle position. Chronology of the timing change is unresolved.

review.notes: Text-identical (goat 504700021 cdb text == pinned modern cards.cdb text) and the errata page (revid 5791183) has only a Japanese lineage, so there is no English printing to date and literal texts are carried on the change. The packet's second upstream entry, 513000028 'Andro Sphinx (Anime)' in cards-unofficial.cdb, is an anime-only version — it Special Summons itself from the Deck, pays no LP, and burns for half the destroyed monster's CURRENT ATK rather than base ATK — so it is not a TCG historical version and is not a baseline candidate. Burn amount is base ATK in both TCG scripts; the reset-constant difference (RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END vs its expansion) is the same bits.
